notes.claim: In an ideal transformer the ratio of secondary to primary voltage equals the ratio of turns in the windings.
The current ratio is the inverse of the voltage ratio; a transformer does not create power or consume it, so power in equals power out in the ideal case.
The ideal case assumes the same flux links every turn of both windings, which is why the voltage ratio follows the turns ratio.

sources.quote: The current ratio in a transformer is the inverse of the ratio for voltage transfor- mation. The transformer does not create power, and it is not designed to consume power.

sources.title: 15.6 Transformers - University Physics Volume 2 | OpenStax
sources.quote: We assume the ideal case for which all magnetic field lines are confined to the core so that the same magnetic flux permeates each turn of both the primary and the secondary windings.
